summary: These two units share 1 motifs: a witness who hears a public adjuration and withholds testimony bears guilt.

passages.text: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى فَٱكْتُبُوهُ وَلْيَكْتُب بَّيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌۢ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَلَا يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَن يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِلِ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلْيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ وَلَا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْـًٔا فَإِن كَانَ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُۥ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱسْتَشْهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمْ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَٱمْرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ وَلَا يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا۟ وَلَا تَسْـَٔمُوٓا۟ أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوْ كَبِيرًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلِهِۦ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا وَأَشْهِدُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ وَلَا يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلَا شَهِيدٌ وَإِن تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَإِنَّهُۥ فُسُوقٌۢ بِكُمْ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

Only in Ammonites and Moabites excluded; Tobiah expelled from the temple; Levites' portions, Sabbath and mixed marriages: The Persian king is called 'king of Babylon'; Temple chambers defiled by an outsider are purified and the holy vessels restored; Children of mixed marriages speak their mother's language and cannot speak Judean; The priesthood and the covenant of the priests and Levites are defiled by mixed marriage; A priest gives a foreign enemy a storeroom in the temple courts as his residence; City gates closed when they grow dark before the Sabbath and opened only after it; A grandson of the high priest is son-in-law of the Samarian governor and is driven away; Unpaid Levites and singers abandon the temple for their fields; Purified Levites guard the city gates to keep the Sabbath holy; Merchants spend the night outside the wall waiting to trade, until threatened away; Reformer curses, strikes and pulls out the hair of the men who married foreign wives; Reformer throws an intruder's household goods out of the temple chamber; and 8 more.

title: The king's question, Nehemiah's commission and the night inspection of the walls ↔ The successful believers who inherit Firdaws
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: royal letter to the keeper of the king's park (pardes) for timber.

passages.note: Royal letter to the keeper of the king's park (pardes) for timber (Asaph, guardian of the pardes (Persian park) supplies timber)
passages.text: וְאִגֶּ֡רֶת אֶל אָסָף֩ שֹׁמֵ֨ר הַפַּרְדֵּ֜ס אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתֶּן לִ֣י עֵצִ֡ים לְ֠קָרוֹת אֶת שַׁעֲרֵ֨י הַבִּירָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר לַבַּ֨יִת֙ וּלְחוֹמַ֣ת הָעִ֔יר וְלַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר אָב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיִּתֶּן לִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כְּיַד אֱלֹהַ֖י הַטּוֹבָ֥ה עָלָֽי

passages.text: ٱلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): echo. al-firdaws ~ ha-pardēs: the same Persian loanword (pairidaēza). In Nehemiah it is the Persian king's timber park with its keeper Asaph (šōmēr ha-pardēs ʾăšer la-mmelekh); in the Quran it is the paradise the believers inherit. A lexical lead, not a shared motif.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Royal letter to the keeper of the king's park (pardes) for timber (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The king's question, Nehemiah's commission and the night inspection of the walls: Builders are accused of rebelling against the imperial king; Jerusalem described to a foreign king as 'the city of my fathers' graves'; A spring at Jerusalem called the Dragon (Tannin) or Jackal Spring; Leader tells the enemies they have no portion, right or memorial in Jerusalem; The queen (shegal) sits beside the king as the courtier makes his request; A courtier fears because his face is sad before the king; King gives letters to governors to grant the traveler safe passage; Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite and Geshem the Arab oppose the rebuilding; Leader secretly inspects the ruined walls by night with a few men; Courtier prays to the God of heaven before answering the king's question; Success attributed to 'the good hand of my God upon me'; Travelers stay three days on arrival before acting; and 1 more.

Only in The successful believers who inherit Firdaws: The righteous inherit al-Firdaws (paradise, from Persian pairidaēza) forever; The faithful guard their private parts except with their wives or those their right hands possess; beyond that is transgression; What the righteous are promised as their inheritance [divergence between the texts]; Entrance liturgy: 'Who may dwell on your holy mountain?' answered by a list of ethical qualifications; The meek / those who wait for YHWH / the righteous and their seed shall inherit the land (yirshu arets).

summary: These two units share 1 motifs: leader prays 'remember me, my god, for good' for his deeds.

passages.note: Leader prays 'remember me, my God, for good' for his deeds
passages.text: זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָ֑ה כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֖יתִי עַל הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): echo. Neh 5:19 zokrâ llî ʾĕlōhay lĕ-ṭôbâ kōl ʾăšer ʿāśîtî: Nehemiah asks God to remember him; Q 2:152 fa-dhkurūnī adhkurkum wa-shkurū lī: God tells the believers to remember him and he will remember them. One-way petition vs mutual remembrance (z-k-r / dh-k-r).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Leader prays 'remember me, my God, for good' for his deeds (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Outcry over debt slavery; Nehemiah's remission and his refusal of the governor's allowance: The poor borrow money against fields and vineyards to pay the king's tax; Parents forced to sell sons and daughters into slavery for debt; In famine the people pledge fields, vineyards and houses for grain; Governor refuses his official food allowance so as not to burden the people; Leader shakes out the fold of his garment: so may God shake out whoever breaks the oath; Governor feeds 150 officials and foreign visitors daily at his own expense; The poor protest: 'our flesh is like our brothers' flesh, our children like their children'; A great outcry of the poor and their wives against their fellow Jews; Alms go to the poor, the needy, the collectors, those whose hearts are reconciled, slaves, debtors, God's cause and the wayfarer; Freeing or buying back the enslaved; Israelite sold to a resident alien may be redeemed by kin or himself, priced by years to jubilee; Lending at interest or increase to a poor brother is forbidden.

Only in The change of qibla: The direction of prayer (qibla) is changed toward the Sacred Mosque; fools ask why; Believers made a middle community (umma wasat), witnesses over mankind, with the messenger a witness over them; God sees the prophet turning his face toward heaven and grants him a qibla he is pleased with; To each a direction he faces: so race toward good deeds; Abraham and Ishmael pray that a messenger be raised from among their offspring; The People of the Book recognize the truth as they recognize their own sons; The direction faced in prayer [divergence between the texts]; Prayers made toward the temple (or toward the land, city and house when in exile) are heard in heaven; Who bears witness to God's oneness [divergence between the texts].

Only in Rebellion after the spies' report and the forty-year sentence: Intercessor argues the nations would say God was unable; Those who slandered the land die by plague; People have tested God 'ten times'; God threatens to destroy a people and put another in its place [divergence between the texts]; People ordered to fight complain to God and wish to be spared the battle; People attack without God's ark or leader and are routed; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; Caleb has 'another spirit' and follows God fully; God offers to destroy the people and make a nation of the hero instead; The townsfolk say 'we augur ill of you' and threaten to stone the messengers; they reply 'your omen is with you'; The people are about to stone their leader; Whole adult generation condemned to die in the desert; only children enter; and 6 more.

title: The Sabbath wood-gatherer; the law of tassels ↔ Covenant at the mountain and the Sabbath-breakers
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: punishment of those who break the sabbath [divergence between the texts].

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Num 27:8-11 ʾîš kî yāmût û-bēn ʾên lô wĕ-haʿăbartem ʾet naḥălātô lĕ-bittô wĕ-ʾim ʾên lô bat ... lĕ-ʾeḥāyw ... la-ʾăḥê ʾābîw ... li-šʾērô ha-qqārōb: a chain of single heirs: son, else daughter, else brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Q 4:11-12 li-dh-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi l-unthayayn ... wa-li-abawayhi li-kulli wāḥidin minhumā s-sudusu ... wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum: fixed fractional shares for several heirs at once, daughters with sons, parents, and spouses (absent from Num 27), siblings only for the kalāla. A sequence of exclusive heirs becomes a set of simultaneous shares. The Quran begins yūṣīkumu llāhu 'God charges you' (cf. ḥuqqat mišpāṭ, 27:11). Num 27:7-8 kēn bĕnôt ṣĕlopḥād dōbĕrōt ... û-bēn ʾên lô wĕ-haʿăbartem ʾet naḥălātô lĕ-bittô: daughters inherit only when there is no son, after a petition; Q 4:11 fa-in kunna nisāʾan fawqa thnatayni fa-lahunna thuluthā mā taraka wa-in kānat wāḥidatan fa-lahā n-niṣf: daughters always inherit, alongside sons at half a son's share, and alone take a half or two-thirds.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Rules for who inherits and in what order or share [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Whether and how daughters inherit [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin (weight 6.3); Daughters petition and win the right to inherit when there is no son (weight 5.8). Pair score 25.0.

Only in Daughters of Zelophehad; Moses views the land; Joshua commissioned: Petition so that a dead man's name not be lost from his clan; Leader ordains his successor by laying hands and sharing his 'splendor' (hod); Decisions sought through the priest's Urim; God addressed as 'God of the spirits of all flesh'; Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin [divergence between the texts]; Blood relatives are nearer to one another (in inheritance) in God's book; Leader defers an unprecedented legal case to a divine oracle; Leader shown the whole land from a mountaintop but may not enter; Prayer that the people not be 'like sheep without a shepherd'; The great leader is denied entry into the promised land for a lapse.

Only in The fixed shares of inheritance: Shares are distributed only after a bequest (waṣiyya) and debts are paid; Inheritance fixed in fractions (one half, a third, a quarter, a sixth, an eighth, two-thirds); Husband and wife inherit fixed shares from each other; Three named daughters (Jemimah, Keziah, Keren-happuch), the most beautiful in the land, inherit among their brothers; Who receives a double share of inheritance [divergence between the texts]; One who dies without parent or child (kalāla): brothers and sisters inherit fixed shares; A son (or brother) inherits the share of two daughters (or sisters); 'These are the bounds (hudud) of God; do not approach (or transgress) them'; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

Outcome: Num 5 lets the bitter water decide, with a physical sign on the guilty body (bə-tēt YHWH ʾet yərēkhēk nōfelet wə-ʾet biṭnēk ṣāvâ); in Q 24:8 the wife's oath alone averts the punishment (wa-yadraʾu ʿanhā l-ʿadhāba an tashhada), with no ordeal, water, dust or written curse, and the verdict is left to God. wə-niqqâ hā-ʾîš mē-ʿāwōn wə-hā-ʾiššâ ha-hîʾ tiśśāʾ ʾet ʿăwōnāh: the accusing husband is free of guilt whatever happens; Q 24:7 wa-l-khāmisatu anna laʿnata llāhi ʿalayhi in kāna mina l-kādhibīna: he invokes God's curse on himself if he is lying.

Pair score 33.5.

Only in The suspected adulteress and the bitter water: Suspected wife's offering is barley flour without oil or frankincense, a 'meal offering of jealousy'; Ordeal curse: the guilty woman's belly swells and her thigh falls; Person responds to an imprecation with 'Amen, amen'; Holy water in an earthen vessel mixed with dust from the sanctuary floor; Husband who brings an ordeal accusation is free of guilt whatever the result; Woman cleared by the ordeal will bear children; A 'spirit of jealousy' comes over a husband who suspects his wife; Priest unbinds the accused woman's hair before God; Written curses are wiped into water that the accused then drinks; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; An oath before God settles a suspicion that cannot be proven.

Only in Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath: The fornicating woman and man each receive a hundred lashes, witnessed by a party of believers; A fornicator may marry only a fornicator or an idolater; such marriage is forbidden to believers; A husband accusing his wife without witnesses swears four times by God and a fifth time invokes God's curse on himself if lying; she averts punishment by four counter-oaths and a fifth invoking God's wrath; Whoever accuses a chaste woman without four witnesses is flogged eighty lashes and his testimony is never accepted; Who is barred from marrying an unchaste woman [divergence between the texts]; Judges told to let no pity hold them back from carrying out a fixed punishment; How many lashes a flogging may have [contrast between the texts]; A man accused swears a curse-oath before the altar, and God judges guilty and innocent; The penalty for adultery or fornication [contrast between the texts]; The penalty for falsely accusing a woman of unchastity [divergence between the texts]; Husband who falsely accuses his bride is flogged, fined 100 silver, and may never divorce her; Adulterer and adulteress both put to death; and 3 more.

title: The suspected adulteress and the bitter water ↔ The annunciation and the mission of Jesus
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke god's curse on the liars.

passages.text: מִ֤י עָלָֽה שָׁמַ֨יִם וַיֵּרַ֡ד מִ֤י אָֽסַף ר֨וּחַ בְּחָפְנָ֡יו מִ֤י צָֽרַר מַ֨יִם בַּשִּׂמְלָ֗ה מִ֭י הֵקִ֣ים כָּל אַפְסֵי אָ֑רֶץ מַה שְּׁמ֥וֹ וּמַֽה שֶּׁם בְּ֝נ֗וֹ כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע

Q: wa-waṣṣaynā l-insāna bi-wālidayhi ... wa-in jāhadāka ʿalā an tushrika bī ... fa-lā tuṭiʿhumā wa-ṣāḥibhumā fī d-dunyā maʿrūfan. The duty to parents is commanded by God, not by the father, and it stops where the parents urge shirk. The mother's part is grounded in pregnancy and two years of nursing (waḥnan ʿalā waḥnin wa-fiṣāluhu fī ʿāmayn), not in her tôrâ.

title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Patience, Safa and Marwa, signs of creation
summary: These two units share 3 motifs: ships go to and fro on the great sea, catalogue of signs: heavens and earth, alternation of night and day, ships, rain reviving dead earth, beasts, winds, clouds, rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites
summary: These two units share 2 motifs: the new moons are time markers for people and for the pilgrimage, sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons.

passages.note: The new moons are time markers for people and for the pilgrimage (Ps 104:19 ʿāśâ yārēaḥ lĕ-môʿădîm: the moon made for appointed times (festivals); Q 2:189 yasʾalūnaka ʿani l-ahillati qul hiya mawāqītu li-n-nāsi wa-l-ḥajj: the new moons are fixed times for people and for the pilgrimage. môʿădîm / mawāqīt, both from roots for 'appointed time'.)

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 35 more.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts]; Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot); God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; God set constellations (buruj) in the sky and adorned it for beholders; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them; Creation is completed in six days; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh); and 1 more.

title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ God's earth is wide; every soul tastes death; signs and the secure sanctuary
summary: These two units share 2 motifs: god provides prey for the lion and food for the raven's young that cry to him, rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Signs for people of understanding; closing prayer

Q: fa-arsalnā ʿalayhimu l-ṭūfāna wa-l-jarāda wa-l-qummala wa-l-ḍafādiʿa wa-l-dama āyātin mufaṣṣalātin, five plagues. Ps 105: hāfakh ʾet-mêmêhem lə-dām ... šāraṣ ʾarṣām ṣəfardəʿîm ... ʿārōv kinnîm ... ʾarbeh. Q's last three, qummal, ḍafādiʿ, dam (lice, frogs, blood), are Exodus's first three (dām, ṣəfardəʿîm, kinnîm) in reverse order. Q adds ṭūfān, which is in no HB list, and leaves out the death of the firstborn (Ps 105:36).

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 25 more.

Q 55: ash-shamsu wa-l-qamaru bi-ḥusbān ... fa-bi-ayyi ālāʾi rabbikumā tukadhdhibān (31 times). Same form and the same first works (heavens, earth, sun, moon). Changed refrain: the psalm affirms (his love endures for ever) and calls Israel to give thanks (hôḏû); the Quran asks a challenge in the dual to jinn and humans: which of your Lord's bounties will you deny? The psalm goes on to Egypt and Israel's history; the Quran to heaven and hell.

evidence.text: Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 14 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Egypt is called 'the tents of Ham' or 'the land of Ham' (weight 6.3); Moses was given nine clear signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Swarms (arov) of insects or wild beasts fill the houses of Egypt (weight 6.3); Quail come up in the evening and cover the camp (weight 6.0); Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs (weight 6.0); God kills every firstborn of the land, from the king's heir to the lowest servant and cattle (weight 6.0); Water brought out of a rock by the leader's rod (weight 6.0); A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus (weight 6.0); God rains bread from heaven to feed the people in the desert (weight 6.0); Nile water is turned to blood (weight 5.8); God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven (weight 5.8); Psalm retells Israel's sacred history (patriarchs, Egypt, wilderness, conquest) as instruction or praise (weight 5.6); Locusts brought by an east wind devour all vegetation left after the hail (weight 5.6); God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night (weight 5.1). Pair score 82.6.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 27 more.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 19 more.
